source.title: Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images with One Multi-Modal Model
source.authors: Chunting Zhou; Lili Yu; Arun Babu; Kushal Tirumala; Michihiro Yasunaga; Leonid Shamis; Jacob Kahn; Xuezhe Ma; Luke Zettlemoyer; Omer Levy

record.tranche_reason: The study measures benchmark performance across model sizes and token counts and fits log-metric versus log-FLOPs trendlines. This is a conceptual test of scaling behavior, using multimodal models and benchmark metrics rather than the original scaling-law setup.
record.gate_note: Figure 5 reports scaling curves and fitted trendlines, but exact datapoint values are not stated in the text. The paper uses FLOPs as a proxy combining parameter count and token count; it does not independently test scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute. Table 3 gives exact results for the largest models. The Chameleon results are the study's own controlled baseline, not results cited from other work.
record.test_reason: Trains Transfusion and a Chameleon baseline at five sizes (0.16B–7B) and fits log-metric vs log-FLOPs trendlines (~1e20–1e22 FLOPs). This is a scaling result in a new mixed-modal setting (text LM loss plus image diffusion). The main aim is comparing methods, and no fit quality or exponents are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that Transfusion scales better than Chameleon on every benchmark, with near-parallel lines and a large gap (e.g. 34× less compute for FID parity). They find that U-Net patch layers improve performance beyond the parameters they add. They also report that a 7B, 2T-token model matches similar-scale diffusion and language models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a multimodal text-and-image setup, compares parameter and data-controlled model families using FLOPs as a proxy, and fits log-metric versus log-FLOPs trendlines. It does not reproduce the original language-model loss sweeps or compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with image patch size, image encoder/decoder architecture, intra-image attention pattern, and diffusion-noise limit; the controlled comparison also uses a different Chameleon training recipe and CFG coefficient from the ablation experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Modality-interface ablations (linear vs U-Net patch layers, intra-image attention, patch size) change image metrics a lot and text perplexity modestly, and the U-Net benefit shrinks with transformer size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In mixed-modal models, image encoder/decoder design and patch compression affect text and image performance, and the effect shrinks with scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Transfusion and Chameleon scaling lines are near-parallel with a constant offset. Parity FLOP ratios range from 0.029 (FID) to 0.600 (Llama accuracy).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the training recipe or modality representation shifts the scaling intercept but not the slope.

record.problems: The scaling-curve datapoints and fitted slopes are not tabulated in the text; Figure 5 provides the curves without exact values. FLOPs combine parameter count and token count, so the study does not isolate their effects. The reported perplexities are benchmark metrics, not an explicit cross-entropy loss report.
record.rows_left_out: No separately tabulated values for the image-generation-literature comparison in Table 9 or image-editing examples were included: those results do not report scaling curves or held-out language-model loss relevant to the tested versions.

untested.parts: Separate scaling in parameters vs tokens; non-bottleneck conditions; several orders of magnitude (only ~2 here); explicit fit quality or exponents.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No depth/width sweep at fixed parameter count.
Video, repeated data and fine-tuning scaling are not tested.
No downstream-vs-loss relation; no fit quality.
No comparison of exponents across setups or fitting methods.

missing.what: Tabulated Transfusion (linear, 2×2) metrics at 0.16B/0.37B/0.76B/1.4B/7B, all at 0.5T tokens. For example, C4 perplexity falls 14.8, 12.0, 10.4, 9.5, 7.7 and FID 37.6, 21.5, 20.3, 19.4, 18.6. These give numeric parameter-scaling data behind Figure 5.
Same per-size series for U-Net variants (C4 perplexity 14.4 to 7.8; CIDEr 15.3 to 33.7).

record.verdict_notes: The scaling fits are used mainly to compare methods; no exponents, R² or extrapolation are reported, and all Figure 5 values are figure-only. Rows r13–r18 are single-size method comparisons and are relinked to none. The V4 rows were relinked to none because U-Net adds parameters and patch size or attention mask are not shape changes at fixed parameter count.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests Wikipedia and C4 perplexity versus combined FLOPs, not cross-entropy directly; it does not independently vary parameters, tokens, and compute or establish the claimed non-bottleneck conditions.
The study compares image encoder/decoder architectures and patch sizes, not depth and width sweeps at fixed parameter count across a wide architecture range.

The study examines image-generation and image-captioning benchmarks in its text-and-image training setting, not image/video modalities generally, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as scaling-law regimes.
The study reports benchmark performance versus FLOPs, not a direct relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
